entries.name: Bandit
entries.use_for: Find common security issues in Python code.
entries.why: The standard Python security linter from PyCQA.
entries.summary: Security linter for Python that analyzes code for common security issues. It is the standard PyCQA static analysis tool used in CI and pre-commit.
entries.best_for: Quick static security checks on Python codebases in CI.
entries.not_for: Python only and pattern-based: it produces false positives and does not check dependencies, secrets or runtime behavior.

entries.name: Checkov
entries.use_for: Scan Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, Dockerfiles and more for security misconfigurations
entries.why: Leading open IaC scanner with 1000+ built-in policies and CI integrations
entries.summary: Static analysis tool for infrastructure as code that also does software composition analysis. Scans Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, Helm, Dockerfile, Bicep, ARM, OpenAPI and more with graph-based policies and 1000+ built-in policies.
entries.best_for: Catching cloud misconfigurations and compliance issues in IaC during CI or pre-commit.
entries.not_for: Static scanning only, no runtime visibility; some advanced features are tied to Prisma Cloud, and policy tuning is needed to cut noise.

entries.name: CrowdSec
entries.use_for: Open-source, crowd-powered intrusion prevention that detects and blocks malicious IPs
entries.why: Modern fail2ban successor with shared blocklists and bouncers for Nginx, Traefik, Cloudflare and more
entries.summary: Open-source IDS/IPS, WAF and bot detection that parses logs, detects attacks and shares malicious IPs through a community blocklist. Detection and remediation are decoupled, with bouncers for firewalls, Nginx, Traefik, Cloudflare and others.
entries.best_for: Protecting self-hosted servers and web apps with crowd-sourced IP blocking, as a modern fail2ban replacement.
entries.not_for: Mostly IP-reputation and log-based; not a full application-layer security suite, and sharing signals with the community network is part of the model.

entries.name: DOMPurify
entries.use_for: Fast, tolerant XSS sanitizer for HTML, MathML and SVG
entries.why: The trusted HTML sanitizer from security firm Cure53; the default fix for rendering untrusted HTML
entries.summary: DOM-only, fast XSS sanitizer for HTML, MathML and SVG, written in JavaScript. Works in modern browsers and, via a DOM implementation, on the server; maintained by security firm Cure53.
entries.best_for: Safely rendering untrusted or user-supplied HTML in the browser.
entries.not_for: Sanitizes markup only; it is not a general security layer, and Node usage needs jsdom or similar. Legacy browsers are unsupported (it does nothing there).

entries.name: Falco
entries.use_for: Cloud-native runtime threat detection for hosts, containers and Kubernetes
entries.why: CNCF graduated project; eBPF-based detection of suspicious behavior at runtime
entries.summary: Cloud-native runtime security agent for Linux that watches kernel events (syscalls) against custom rules and enriches them with container and Kubernetes metadata, alerting on suspicious behavior. CNCF graduated project.
entries.best_for: Real-time threat detection on hosts, containers and Kubernetes clusters.
entries.not_for: Detection and alerting only, not prevention or blocking; Linux only and needs rule tuning and a downstream SIEM or alert pipeline.

entries.name: Gitleaks
entries.use_for: Detect hardcoded secrets like API keys and passwords in git repos and files.
entries.why: The most popular open-source secret scanner, easy to run in pre-commit and CI.
entries.summary: Tool that detects hardcoded secrets such as API keys and passwords in git repositories and files, easy to run in pre-commit and CI. The README says it is feature complete and receives only security patches, with the author's focus moving to Betterleaks.
entries.best_for: Scanning repos and history for leaked secrets in CI or pre-commit hooks.
entries.not_for: Maintenance mode (no new features per its README); it detects but does not verify whether a secret is live, unlike Kingfisher.

entries.name: Grype
entries.use_for: Vulnerability scanner for container images, filesystems and SBOMs
entries.why: Fast, accurate CVE scanning that pairs with Syft SBOMs; easy to drop into CI
entries.summary: Vulnerability scanner for container images, filesystems and SBOMs. Supports major OS and language ecosystems and Docker, OCI and Singularity formats, and prioritizes findings with EPSS, KEV and risk scoring; pairs with Syft SBOMs.
entries.best_for: Fast CVE scanning in CI for images and dependencies.
entries.not_for: Reports known vulnerabilities only: no secrets, IaC or runtime analysis, and results depend on the vulnerability database.

entries.name: Helmet
entries.use_for: Secure Express/Node apps by setting HTTP security headers like CSP and HSTS
entries.why: Standard one-line hardening middleware for Express, with millions of weekly downloads
entries.summary: Express/Node middleware that sets HTTP security response headers such as Content-Security-Policy and Strict-Transport-Security. app.use(helmet()) sets 13 headers by default.
entries.best_for: One-line baseline header hardening for Express and Connect-style Node apps.
entries.not_for: Headers only: does not replace input validation, auth or CSRF protection. Default CSP may need tuning, and it targets Node middleware stacks.

entries.name: Kingfisher
entries.use_for: Detect secrets in code and history and validate whether they are live.
entries.why: MongoDB-maintained scanner that adds live validation and blast-radius mapping.
entries.summary: Rust secret scanner maintained by MongoDB that detects leaked secrets with hundreds of built-in rules, validates which credentials are live, maps the blast radius of each leak and helps revoke exposed secrets. Apache-2.0.
entries.best_for: Secret scanning that tells you which found credentials are actually active, across code and history.
entries.not_for: Live validation makes outbound calls to providers, which needs care in sensitive environments; newer than gitleaks or trufflehog.

entries.name: Lynis
entries.use_for: Audit Linux, macOS and Unix hosts for security hardening and compliance.
entries.why: Long-standing, agentless host auditing tool with actionable hardening suggestions.
entries.summary: Security auditing tool for Unix-based systems (Linux, macOS, BSD) that runs on the host itself. It performs an in-depth scan of system configuration, installed packages and defenses, then reports findings with hardening suggestions.
entries.best_for: Sysadmins and auditors checking Linux/Unix servers for hardening and compliance gaps (e.g. before audits), without installing agents.
entries.not_for: Not a network or web-app vulnerability scanner and not for Windows hosts. Output is advice to act on manually; it does not auto-remediate. Some features are in the paid Lynis Enterprise.

entries.name: Nuclei
entries.use_for: Scan web apps, APIs and infrastructure for vulnerabilities using YAML templates.
entries.why: Fast template-driven scanner with a huge community template library.
entries.summary: Vulnerability scanner driven by simple YAML templates that describe detection steps for HTTP, DNS, TCP, SSL, WHOIS and other protocols. A large community template library ships with it, and scans run in parallel with request clustering.
entries.best_for: Scanning web apps, APIs and infrastructure for known CVEs and misconfigurations, writing custom checks, and running regression scans in CI/CD.
entries.not_for: Detects what templates cover; it is not a code analyzer or full manual pentest tool. Scanning targets you do not own is illegal, and results depend on template quality.

entries.name: OSV-Scanner
entries.use_for: Find known vulnerabilities in your project's dependencies using the OSV database.
entries.why: Google's SCA scanner backed by the open, multi-ecosystem OSV.dev database.
entries.summary: CLI frontend to the OSV.dev vulnerability database and OSV-Scalibr. It reads lockfiles, SBOMs and project dependency lists across many languages and package managers and reports known vulnerabilities affecting them.
entries.best_for: Software composition analysis in CI or locally: finding known vulnerable dependencies across multi-language repos using an open database.
entries.not_for: Only finds known, published vulnerabilities in dependencies; it does not analyze your own code for bugs (use a SAST tool) or scan running hosts.

entries.name: OWASP Nettacker
entries.use_for: Automate network and web reconnaissance and vulnerability scanning.
entries.why: OWASP-maintained modular scanning framework; Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: OWASP Python framework for automated network and web reconnaissance and vulnerability scanning. It uses modular scan and brute-force modules, supports multiple targets and outputs, and can run from CLI, API or Docker.
entries.best_for: Automating information gathering, port/service scans and basic vulnerability checks during authorized penetration tests or security assessments.
entries.not_for: Intended only for authorized testing; not a defensive monitoring or code-scanning tool. Coverage and accuracy are narrower than commercial scanners.

entries.name: Semgrep
entries.use_for: Scan source code for bugs and security issues with fast, customizable pattern rules.
entries.why: Lightweight, multi-language SAST with a large rule registry; CE is LGPL-2.1.
entries.summary: Static analysis tool that searches code with patterns that look like the source language itself rather than ASTs or regexes. Supports 30+ languages, a large rule registry, and runs in the IDE, pre-commit hooks or CI.
entries.best_for: Fast SAST in CI and pre-commit: custom bug and security rules, enforcing coding standards, and finding insecure patterns across many languages.
entries.not_for: Community Edition analyzes within single files/functions, so it misses cross-file data-flow issues that the paid platform handles. LGPL-2.1 core; some rules have separate licenses.

entries.name: SkillSpector
entries.use_for: Scan AI agent skills for vulnerabilities, malicious patterns and risky behavior before installing.
entries.why: NVIDIA-maintained scanner for the agent-skill supply chain; Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: Security scanner for AI agent skills (as used by Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI). It analyzes skill packages for vulnerabilities, malicious patterns and risky behavior before they are installed, as part of NVIDIA's verified-skills pipeline.
entries.best_for: Vetting third-party agent skills before installing them, or adding a pre-install safety check to an agent skill supply chain.
entries.not_for: Scoped to agent skills only; it is not a general code, dependency or container scanner. Heuristic detection cannot guarantee a skill is safe.

entries.name: Syft
entries.use_for: Generate SBOMs (SPDX, CycloneDX) from container images and filesystems
entries.why: The most used open SBOM generator; the foundation for supply-chain scanning pipelines
entries.summary: CLI tool and Go library that generates a Software Bill of Materials from container images, filesystems and archives. Supports many packaging ecosystems and image formats, and outputs CycloneDX, SPDX or Syft JSON.
entries.best_for: Producing SBOMs for images and repos in CI, and as the input to a vulnerability scanner such as Grype.
entries.not_for: Only inventories packages; it does not find vulnerabilities by itself (pair with Grype or Trivy). Not a runtime monitoring tool.

entries.name: Trivy
entries.use_for: Scan containers, filesystems, repos, IaC and Kubernetes for vulnerabilities and misconfigurations.
entries.why: All-in-one, widely adopted scanner that drops easily into CI; Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: Versatile scanner that targets container images, filesystems, remote git repos, VM images and Kubernetes. It finds vulnerable OS and language packages, IaC misconfigurations, secrets and license issues, and can generate SBOMs.
entries.best_for: One tool in CI for container, IaC and dependency scanning across Docker, Kubernetes and repos.
entries.not_for: Detection depth per area is shallower than specialized tools (dedicated SAST, secrets verification, DAST). It is not a runtime protection or web-app pentest tool.

entries.name: TruffleHog
entries.use_for: Find, verify and analyze leaked credentials in git, CI, cloud storage and more
entries.why: Verifies detected secrets against live APIs to cut false positives; 800+ detectors
entries.summary: Secrets scanner that finds leaked credentials in git history, CI, cloud storage, chat and other sources. It has 800+ detectors and verifies findings against live APIs to reduce false positives, plus can analyze key permissions.
entries.best_for: Auditing repos and org data for leaked API keys and passwords, pre-commit/CI secret scanning, and incident response on suspected leaks.
entries.not_for: Only looks for secrets, not code or dependency vulnerabilities. Verification makes live calls to third-party APIs, which may be unwanted. Enterprise features are separate.

entries.name: Vuls
entries.use_for: Scan Linux/FreeBSD servers, containers and libraries for known CVEs without agents.
entries.why: Agentless vulnerability scanner for server fleets with multiple data sources.
entries.summary: Agentless vulnerability scanner for Linux and FreeBSD written in Go. It checks servers, containers and libraries against multiple vulnerability data sources and reports known CVEs over SSH without installing software on targets.
entries.best_for: Teams managing fleets of Linux/FreeBSD servers who want agentless CVE reporting and notifications.
entries.not_for: Report-only: it does not update vulnerable packages. Not for Windows or web-app testing, and requires setting up vulnerability databases.

entries.name: ZAP
entries.use_for: Test web applications for vulnerabilities with an intercepting proxy and automated scans.
entries.why: The most widely used free DAST tool, scriptable and CI-friendly.
entries.summary: ZAP (Zed Attack Proxy) by Checkmarx is a free, open source web app security scanner. It automatically finds security vulnerabilities in web applications during development and testing, and also supports manual testing by pentesters. Apache 2.0 licensed.
entries.best_for: Scanning your own web applications for vulnerabilities during development or CI, and manual penetration testing.
entries.not_for: Static code analysis or dependency scanning; it tests running web apps. Only scan applications you are authorized to test.
